_about: Recorded starting bill numbers and numbering periods (decision OCD-LEG-NUM-002). Only values a source states are built; inferred ones stay UNKNOWN and those chambers start at 1. Approved by Claude CTO, 03 PROJECT LANES, Sept 28, 2026 01:16 EDT. Quotes are search excerpts of the named pages; the pages could not be fetched directly.

starts.quote: House Bills in Arizona are numbered starting with 2001 and designated "H.B."
Senate Bills are numbered starting 1001 and designated "S.B." (supported by https://www.azleg.gov/legtext/56leg/1R/bills/SB1001S.pdf)
House bills are assigned four-digit bill numbers, starting with the number "1001"... if a House bill were introduced as "1234", that would designate the 234th House bill

Senate bills are assigned three-digit numbers, starting with the number "001". (Numbers are year-prefixed, e.g. HB25-1001, and reset each session. A special session uses a letter suffix, e.g. HB25B-1001.)
Senate bills are numbered from 1 to 5000, House bills from 5001 to 9999.
Senate bills are numbered from 1 to 5000, House bills from 5001 to 9999.

Senate bills start numbering at number one, and House bills start at 1000. (The snippet says 1000, but the observed first bill is House Bill 1001 in every session: iga.in.gov/legislative/2021, 2023 and 2026 bills/house/1001, so the first number used is 1001.)
Senate bills start numbering at number one
House bills (HB) start at number 2001 and Senate bills (SB) start at number 1. ... These numbers will continue into the second year of the biennium.
Senate bills (SB) start at number 1. ... These numbers will continue into the second year of the biennium.

House bills in the Michigan legislature begin with House Bill No. 4001 and Senate bills are numbered starting with Senate Bill No. 1. (search summary: this applies to each two-year session, meaning the even year continues the sequence)
Senate bills are numbered starting with Senate Bill No. 1.
House bills begin with the number 1001, and Senate bills begin with the number 2001.
House bills begin with the number 1001, and Senate bills begin with the number 2001.

Numbering of Senate bills begins at 1 and numbering of House bills begins at 3000. (Snippet says 3000, not 3001. Bill list page 'List of 2017-2018 House Bills 3000 - 3199' at scstatehouse.gov covers both years, which suggests the numbers continue through the two-year session. That is inferred.)
Numbering of Senate bills begins at 1 and numbering of House bills begins at 3000.
Senate bills and resolutions begin with the number 1 and are printed on yellow paper; House bills and resolutions begin with the number 1001 and are printed on blue paper
Senate bills and resolutions begin with the number 1

House bills (HB) are numbered starting with 1000 at the beginning of each biennium ... The numbering ranges are 1000-3999 for House bills (search-engine summary of leg.wa.gov help pages; numbering belongs to the biennium, so the even-year session continues the sequence instead of restarting)
Senate bills (SB) are numbered starting with 5000 at the beginning of each biennium ... 5000-7999 for Senate bills. Each bill number is associated with that bill for one legislative biennium
